title: K-Means as the Zero-Temperature Limit of Normalized RBF Assignments: Rates, Trajectories, and Exact Recovery with Entmax
summary: K-Means is usually treated as a discrete procedure outside gradient-based learning, whereas normalized radial basis function (RBF) layers are smooth. We make precise the sense in which K-Means is the zero-temperature limit of such a layer. Relaxing the K-Means assignments to the simplex with a Shannon entropy penalty yields the normalized Gaussian RBF responsibilities and a reduced objective $F_σ$ with $0\le J-F_σ\le 2nσ^2\log k$, so $F_σ$ $Γ$-converges to the K-Means distortion $J$.
